keyResults.definition: 100% of changed repositories have clean exact-head review, zero unresolved threads, and green protected-main checks.
100% of accepted portfolio manifests pin component version, exact revision, evidence digest, and replay method.
Zero moved immutable tags and zero contradictory, altered, or mismatched proofs accepted.
E1 names one target user or buyer problem, one bounded workflow, measures, controls, stop conditions, and a disposition by the end of Portfolio 2026.10.
The scorecard keeps OBSERVED and SYNTHETIC evidence separate and measures proposal time, review effort, comprehension, replay, and willingness to continue.
Zero credentials, customer data, paid services, cloud writes, or operational authority are required for evaluation readiness.
Exactly one authorized AWS/Azure foundation profile passes and every unsafe fixture fails closed.
100% of plan, apply, verify, rollback, and teardown stages retain exact-revision, digest-bound evidence.
Teardown leaves zero managed residual resources and recorded spend does not exceed the authorized ceiling.
Zero AI or component self-approvals.

A versioned successor maps 100% of valid Objectives, Key Results, Epics, Features, Stories, candidate tasks, stable identifiers, relationships, totals, and fail-closed consistency rules while preserving valid Guard V1 behavior.
Console presents 100% of accepted producer evidence without recreating Guard policy or blending OBSERVED and SYNTHETIC results.
By August 2027, the pilot decision packet covers SLOs, support, recovery, privacy, security, cost, publication, and accountable authority and records RELEASE, HOLD, or STOP.

100% of portfolio products have an explicit supported or deliberately gated adoption surface and ownership boundary: Guard App; Forge App + worker; Console OCI/Compose with Helm separately gated; first-class Storefront app + Backstage Adapter; Assurance customer-hosted decision; Composite AI embedded runtime.

Guard and Forge have reversible install/upgrade/uninstall evidence, Console has a reproducible customer-hosted evaluation package, Storefront has a customer-hosted standalone app plus reusable Backstage Adapter over one order contract, and no distribution path grants cloud execution or self-approval authority.

100% of released customer-hosted packages or accepted app surfaces have explicit exact version/revision, digest/provenance status, dependency/SBOM status, upgrade/rollback procedure where applicable, retained acceptance evidence, and cross-product compatibility coordinates; the minimum status profile is accepted while missing product-specific SBOM/signing evidence remains explicitly absent or gated rather than inferred.
100% of active GitHub integration code uses configurable web/API endpoints and contains zero mandatory hard-coded GitHub SaaS endpoints in runtime paths.

At least one authorized GHES target passes App registration/installation, webhook verification, installation-token authentication, immutable repository reads, PR/Check/evidence flows, and version/capability detection before GHES support is claimed.
All GHES-targeted Actions paths run on self-hosted runners, and deterministic core operation has a restricted-network profile with optional external AI adapters disabled by default.
Standard network-enabled foundation orders require zero consumer-supplied raw CIDRs, route-table identifiers, DNS zone identifiers, resolver endpoints, or firewall rules
Every live address allocation is bound to an authoritative customer-approved IPAM source or approved allocation service, and conflicting or ambiguous allocations fail closed
Every live DNS dependency is bound to an approved namespace/zone reference, owner, lifecycle policy, logging expectation, and resolution profile before mutation

Standard approved network profiles can be fulfilled without per-order network-engineer intervention; all material changes and exceptions are routed to accountable network/security authorities with retained evidence
Standard foundation orders require zero consumer-authored IAM policy JSON, raw firewall rules, KMS identifiers, secret-store credentials, or security-event destination identifiers
Every live foundation instance is bound to an approved, versioned SecurityProfile whose required controls are validated before any authorized mutation
Every security-profile exception is target-specific, time-bounded, attributable, separately approved, and retained with compensating-control and removal evidence
Console can present the selected security profile, control status, evidence references, exceptions, and accountable owners without recreating Guard policy or granting execution authority
Standard foundation orders require zero consumer-supplied cloud access keys, client secrets, service-account keys, raw trust policies, or raw IAM policy documents
Every live workload identity is bound to an approved, versioned IdentityProfile with exact issuer/subject/audience/target constraints and no static long-lived cloud credentials in the reference path

Discovery, execution, approval, evidence, and AI identities remain distinct, and any privilege escalation or wildcard trust fails closed unless covered by a separately approved, time-bounded exception

Console can present identity profile, effective-permission evidence, federation binding, revocation status, access-review references, and accountable owners without exposing credential material or granting access authority
Standard approved placement profiles can be fulfilled without per-order cloud-governance engineering; material changes and exceptions are routed to accountable authorities
Standard foundation orders require zero consumer-supplied cloud account, subscription, project, folder, management-group, billing-account, or organization-unit identifiers
Every target is bound to an approved hierarchy profile, accountable owner, environment boundary, billing relationship, quota profile, and immutable placement evidence before any authorized mutation
Unsupported hierarchy, region, billing, ownership, policy, or quota combinations fail closed
Every authorized foundation instance has an approved observability profile with required audit, metrics, logging, alerting, retention, and ownership references
Standard orders require zero consumer-supplied raw logging endpoints, monitoring workspace IDs, alert destinations, or provider-specific telemetry configuration
Missing required telemetry, disabled audit paths, unknown destinations, or profile mismatch fails closed for live stages
Console can present product health, telemetry coverage, evidence references, and accountable owners without becoming the source monitoring system or policy engine
Every stateful live foundation product has an explicit approved resilience profile or an attributable NOT_APPLICABLE decision
Standard orders require zero consumer-supplied raw backup-vault IDs, replication rules, provider failover configuration, or storage-retention machinery
Missing recovery ownership, incompatible RTO/RPO, absent required backup/replication, or untested teardown/recovery conditions fail closed for applicable live stages
Pilot-readiness evidence includes restore/recovery tests, failure behavior, ownership, and observed recovery results rather than configuration claims alone
Every authorized foundation instance has accountable cost ownership, allocation metadata, an approved budget/cost ceiling, and lifecycle cost evidence
Standard orders require zero consumer-supplied raw billing-account controls, unrestricted quota changes, or provider-specific budget implementation
Missing cost ownership, absent ceiling, unsupported quota, altered allocation metadata, or unauthorized spending path fails closed before applicable live execution
Console can present cost ownership, approved ceiling, observed spend, anomalies, and lifecycle cost evidence without becoming the billing authority
Public Preview deployments remain isolated and clearly labeled while separate customer-hosted Connected Storefront and Forge profiles are implemented
One authenticated, integrity-bound Storefront → Forge transport preserves the accepted handoff semantics and human-review stop
Connected Storefront and Forge expose bounded adapter/readiness and provenance state without exposing secrets or claiming Operational maturity
Cross-product synthetic acceptance proves preview isolation, transport authentication, tamper rejection, and zero autonomous approval/provisioning authority
AI authoring may propose requirements, evidence mappings, and product mappings only against versioned inputs and explicit human acceptance
Agent operations remain constrained by deterministic policy, least privilege, human approval boundaries, revocation/rollback, and retained evidence
No agent-operated capability advances to Operational status before customer-selected validation and explicit authority
100% of customer-scoped contracts selected for the bounded journey carry explicit customer, organization, and environment context and reject missing or conflicting scope.
Synthetic cross-customer substitution tests reject 100% of mismatched trusted profiles, approvals, evidence packages, product/order bindings, and assurance records across the bounded product journey.
The target architecture documents tenant-scoped identity, secrets, integrations, custody, audit, versioning, lifecycle, recovery, and incident boundaries with no implicit cross-customer authority.
Dedicated-enterprise and managed-isolated acceptance profiles are documented and validated before any shared multi-tenant SaaS claim; shared tenancy remains separately gated.
change-context contract: define an organization-neutral, versioned Change Readiness Package with explicit current/desired/delta/evidence/missing-field semantics

Retained relationship history: define and prove tenant-scoped temporal relationship history sufficient to reconstruct product/component/dependency/change relationships without creating a shadow enterprise CMDB
Deterministic delta and export: produce repeatable before/after, network/security/dependency deltas and starter exports whose claims are bound to exact retained inputs
Human-governance handoff: prove that organization-specific submission/approval fields remain explicit and that export never creates approval, authorization, risk acceptance or execution authority
100% of domain capabilities consumed through EP-22 bind the exact domain, capability revision, trusted profile/version/digest, system, scope, and accountable domain authority before acceptance.

The Networking reference proves one provider-neutral capability can be consumed by an infrastructure product without transferring network-policy ownership or requiring consumer-authored raw network implementation identifiers.
MANUAL, ASSISTED, and AUTOMATED execution modes preserve the same capability contract, approval binding, evidence requirements, and separately authorized executor boundary.

Pending, expired, superseded, withdrawn, mismatched, tampered, incomplete, or outside-envelope states fail closed; outside-envelope requests require explicit domain exception handling and never self-approve.

headlineKeyResults.title: Accepted changes and releases remain review-clean and immutable

epicContributions.description: Locks accepted changes and releases to immutable evidence, reviewed digests, and custody records so accepted state cannot drift silently.

headlineKeyResults.title: Accepted evidence is reproducible from exact pinned inputs

epicContributions.description: Retains exact pinned inputs, digests, and replayable evidence needed to reproduce accepted findings independently.

headlineKeyResults.title: Evaluation demonstrates a bounded, measurable user outcome

epicContributions.description: Defines the scorecard and bounded evaluation criteria used to demonstrate whether the evaluator produces a measurable user outcome.
Provides trusted evidence intake and assessment-package inputs so evaluation results are grounded in verifiable evidence rather than assertion.

headlineKeyResults.title: Evaluation readiness requires zero operational authority or sensitive runtime dependency

epicContributions.description: Keeps the evaluation profile synthetic and planning-only, explicitly excluding operational authority and sensitive runtime dependencies.

headlineKeyResults.title: Consumers request governed foundation outcomes without provider-specific implementation knowledge

epicContributions.description: Presents provider-neutral network products so consumers request connectivity outcomes instead of authoring cloud-specific network configuration.
Packages approved security and policy profiles so consumers request security outcomes without designing provider-specific controls.
Exposes identity and federation profiles as governed products so consumers do not author trust policies or credential mechanics.
Turns hierarchy and tenant vending into bounded products so consumers request resource scopes without provider-specific hierarchy knowledge.
Provides provider-neutral observability profiles so consumers request telemetry outcomes without supplying vendor-specific endpoints or workspace identifiers.
Adds a replaceable enterprise telemetry adapter so Splunk-specific transport and routing stay behind the platform instead of leaking into consumer requests.
Productizes resilience and recovery outcomes so consumers select recovery requirements without designing provider-specific backup or failover mechanics.
Productizes cost and FinOps controls so consumers request governed cost outcomes without wiring provider-specific billing or budget configuration.
Lets domain authorities publish governed capability contracts so consumers receive approved infrastructure outcomes without inheriting domain-specific implementation mechanics.

headlineKeyResults.title: Every authorized foundation is bound to approved profiles, accountable ownership, and lifecycle evidence

epicContributions.description: Binds minimum-foundation instances to approved profiles, accountable owners, lifecycle state, and evidence before they can advance.
Binds network products to approved connectivity profiles, accountable ownership, lifecycle expectations, and retained validation evidence.
Attaches security products to approved policy profiles, accountable ownership, lifecycle constraints, and evidence references.
Binds identity products to approved federation and role profiles, accountable owners, trust versions, and retained evidence.
Binds hierarchy and vending products to approved naming, ownership, quota, policy, and lifecycle profiles with retained evidence.
Binds observability products to approved logging, metrics, alerting, retention profiles, accountable owners, and coverage evidence.
Preserves tenant-scoped routing, destination profile, redaction rules, and evidence references when telemetry leaves IPW for Splunk.
Binds resilience products to approved recovery objectives, accountable ownership, lifecycle expectations, and observed recovery evidence.
Binds FinOps products to approved cost policies, accountable ownership, budget expectations, and retained cost evidence.
Binds each consumed capability to exact trusted profile, revision, system, scope, accountable owner, evidence requirements, and an explicit execution-maturity mode.

headlineKeyResults.title: Unsafe, unsupported, or unauthorized foundation states fail closed without self-approval

epicContributions.description: Rejects unsupported or unauthorized minimum-foundation states and keeps human authorization outside the product itself.
Fails closed on policy mismatch, missing required security controls, or unsupported security states without self-approval.
Fails closed on invalid trust, excessive privilege, missing identity bindings, or unsupported federation state without granting access.
Fails closed when required telemetry, audit paths, destinations, or observability profiles are missing or invalid.
Fails closed on unknown telemetry destinations, cross-tenant routing, invalid trust, redaction violations, or malformed Splunk delivery state.
Fails closed when recovery prerequisites or evidence are missing rather than implying resilience from configuration alone.
Fails closed on missing cost-governance evidence or unsupported spending paths instead of silently accepting unmanaged cost exposure.
Fails closed on invalid hierarchy, ownership, naming, quota, or policy state instead of vending an unauthorized resource scope.
Fails closed on stale, superseded, mismatched, incomplete, tampered, or outside-envelope capability state and routes exceptions back to accountable domain authority.

headlineKeyResults.title: Decision surfaces present trustworthy operational evidence without becoming the source authority

epicContributions.description: Supplies verified assessment and evidence packages to decision surfaces without making the viewer the source of truth.
Structures planning and outcome evidence for review while preserving authoritative producer and decision boundaries.
Aggregates readiness evidence for a release or pilot decision without granting approval or operational authority.
Projects security status and evidence references to decision surfaces while policy authority remains with approved profiles and owners.
Projects identity and trust status plus evidence references for review without turning the viewer into an IAM authority.
Projects telemetry coverage, health, and ownership evidence to Console without making Console the monitoring or policy authority.
Returns Splunk delivery health, routing state, and evidence references to Console while Splunk remains an observation destination, not authority.

headlineKeyResults.title: Operational readiness is proven through recoverability, cost evidence, and accountable release decisions

epicContributions.description: Defines the explicit release, hold, or stop decision gate using accumulated operational evidence and accountable ownership.
Provides recoverability evidence needed to judge whether the product can be operated and restored safely.
Provides authoritative cost and FinOps evidence needed to judge whether the product is economically operable and governed.

headlineKeyResults.title: Planning and change context remain versioned, reconstructable, and handoff-ready

epicContributions.description: Keeps desired outcomes, planning assumptions, and decision context versioned so later change packages can be reconstructed.
Builds retained current and desired-state history, dependency relationships, deterministic deltas, and handoff-ready change-readiness packages.
Transforms the frozen IPW request and evidence context into a tenant-scoped ServiceNow workflow handoff while keeping approval fields explicit and execution separate.

headlineKeyResults.title: Products have reversible, evidence-backed adoption paths in customer-controlled environments

epicContributions.description: Provides documented, reversible distribution and adoption paths so products can be installed and evaluated in customer-controlled environments.
Defines restricted-network and GHES portability paths that let customers adopt the portfolio without depending on public-SaaS-only execution.

headlineKeyResults.title: Compatibility and support claims remain provenance-bound and require authorized live validation

epicContributions.description: Binds compatibility and support claims to exact release and dependency evidence rather than broad marketing assertions.
Requires authorized live GHES or customer-runner evidence before claiming support beyond the bounded synthetic portability baseline.

headlineKeyResults.title: Connected product flow is isolated, authenticated, and integrity-bound

epicContributions.description: Connects Storefront and Forge through authenticated, digest-bound transport while preserving preview isolation and tamper rejection.

headlineKeyResults.title: Connected operation exposes readiness and provenance while preserving zero autonomous authority

epicContributions.description: Surfaces adapter readiness, provenance, evidence state, and the human-review stop while keeping all autonomous execution authority false.
Carries connected requests into ServiceNow and verifies returned decisions against exact request, product, and evidence bindings without treating workflow approval as provisioning authority.

headlineKeyResults.title: AI-assisted authoring stays bound to versioned inputs and explicit human acceptance

epicContributions.description: Allows AI to propose requirements, mappings, and product configurations only against versioned inputs with explicit human acceptance.

headlineKeyResults.title: Agent operation remains least-privileged, reversible, evidenced, and gated before Operational use

epicContributions.description: Constrains future agent actions with deterministic policy, least privilege, rollback and revocation, retained evidence, and operational gating.

headlineKeyResults.title: Customer scope and cross-customer isolation fail closed throughout the bounded journey

epicContributions.description: Propagates customer, organization, and environment scope through identity, profiles, evidence, approvals, products, secrets, integrations, and audit with cross-customer substitution tests.

headlineKeyResults.title: Tenant authority, custody, and deployment boundaries are explicit before any shared-tenancy claim

epicContributions.description: Defines explicit tenant authority, custody, deployment, and isolation boundaries that must be proven before any shared-tenancy claim.
